clue.text: Pill getting cold in a very hot sauce

parts.note: a tab is slang for a tablet or pill

indicators.note: the cold letter sits inside the a-plus-very pair

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone takes a pill with a chilli-fiery sauce, cold set against heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'very hot' looks like one phrase describing the sauce, but 'a very' gives letters and 'hot sauce' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a trademarked fiery chilli condiment from Louisiana.

clue.text: Short tweet getting through, it's felt

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trill is a bird's warbling tweet
by means through, as in 'by means of'

explanation.surface: A bird's brief tweet getting through, and it is emotionally felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'felt' is the fabric, not an emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft hat traditionally made of felt.

clue.text: See 8
Elastic persisting, most flexible

indicators.note: elastic means stretchable, so the letters are pulled into a new shape

explanation.surface: Elastic that keeps going is the bendiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Springiest is the superlative of springy, bouncy and resilient.

clue.text: King Lear's opening, rubbish

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia

indicators.note: opening means the first letter

explanation.surface: Dismissing the first lines of Shakespeare's tragedy as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear looks like the Shakespeare king, but the king is Offa.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal can mean waste or refuse, as well as animal innards.

clue.text: Meteorological formation right in position

indicators.note: the right letter is placed inside the word for position

parts.note: status is standing or position

explanation.surface: A weather formation sitting exactly where it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, flat, grey layer of cloud, a formation studied by weather forecasters.

clue.text: Jaguar ultimately has spotted coat? Grab one that's plain

indicators.note: the word for spotted wraps round the last letter of the big cat

parts.note: spotted means seen

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the cat is used

parts.note: to get is to grab
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spotted big cat's coat, and a grab at an animal on the plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; the Serengeti is a vast plain in Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a famous East African grassland, a vast plain.

clue.text: Centre dismissed in game — red!

indicators.note: the central letter of the game is sent off

parts.note: rugby is a game

explanation.surface: A rugby centre sent off: shown a red card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; centre is a rugby position, but here it is the middle letter of RUGBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a deep red colour, after the gemstone.

clue.text: Trapped by bear, a tiger briefly leaves container

indicators.note: the bear holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A tiger, caught by a bear, makes its escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is tea leaves, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small tin or box for storing tea leaves.

clue.text: Start to dig the salt of the earth, among other things, as possible building material

indicators.note: the following letters go in the midst of the word for other things

parts.note: sundries are miscellaneous items

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken from dig

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: Digging the earth's salt as a potential construction material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a brick' is British slang for a decent, dependable person, the salt of the earth; 'Start to' is the indicator, not a verb meaning begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks of clay baked in sunshine have long served as a building resource.

clue.text: I drink when disheartened, as more aloof

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the drink is dropped

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: Someone drinks when glum, and so becomes even more standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle D out of CIDER, leaving CIER; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy describes a cold, distant manner, so the comparative means colder in manner.

clue.text: Some thinker, supporter kept in check by government department

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a UK government department

indicators.note: the supporting garment is held inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A thinker whose backer is restrained by Whitehall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some thinker' means part of a thinker: the front portion of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The forebrain is a part of the brain, so it is some of a thinking organ.

clue.text: Vehicle tours doubly popular around the middle of Basildon, area untouched by the sun

indicators.note: the vehicle goes round everything that follows

parts.note: a bike is a two-wheeled vehicle

indicators.note: the two popular words wrap round the central letters of the town
doubly means the word for popular is written twice

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the central pair of letters of the eight-letter town name

explanation.surface: A cyclist doing laps of an Essex town that never sees sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: Basildon is a town in Essex. 'tours' and 'around' are both containers, nested one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin along the edge of swimwear briefs stays covered when sunbathing, so it remains pale.

clue.text: Pretty light

definitions.meaning: pale in colour, as of hair or skin

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means both attractive and pale-coloured, as with blond hair.

clue.text: Hot fashion in order around 2000, describing spectacles, perhaps

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the number
to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: MM is 2000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Hot styles from around the year 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges IN ORDER into ORNRIED, which goes around MM.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses with frames of horn or imitation horn are so described, an example of an eyewear style.

clue.text: I don't know how I make money with debts

indicators.note: to make something out of letters is to build a new word by reworking them

explanation.surface: A baffled person confessing they have no idea how they earn while in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' and 'with' are links; 'make' turns I, MONEY and DEBTS into one pool of letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom confessing that something is too hard to understand.

clue.text: Low-fat mayo, perhaps — dive in naked!

definitions.meaning: a reduced-fat dressing could jokingly be called a slim sauce for dunking
to plunge into water without clothes on

explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, 'skinny' (low-fat) plus 'dip' (a sauce like mayo) describes a slimline dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming nude is the idiomatic sense, and a low-fat sauce is the playful literal sense.

clue.text: Counter, on top of which room key

indicators.note: in a down entry the room word sits above the counter word

parts.note: room means space
a bar is a counter in a pub

explanation.surface: A pub counter with a room key left on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key at the bottom of a keyboard inserts a gap between words.

clue.text: Swop tailored clothing passion for sporty trousers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters dress, or enclose, the passion word
tailored means cut and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: lust is a strong passion

explanation.surface: Exchanging made-to-measure clothing for golfing trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'clothing' is a verb, the shuffled letters dressing the passion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggy knickerbockers worn for golf, so they are trousers for sport.

clue.text: Middle Eastern nirvana in it's elapsed, somewhat in recession

indicators.note: in recession says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A meditative bliss has passed, fading into the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Palestine, a territory in the Middle East, so the word is an adjective of that region.

clue.text: Head in miniature, wee like a mouse

indicators.note: the leading letter of the following word

parts.note: wee is informal for urine

explanation.surface: A tiny head and small, a mouse-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like small, but it is urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Murine is the zoological adjective for mice and rats.

clue.text: Unrelenting influence of children, affectedly proper and sweet

indicators.note: affectedly means in an artificial manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children working their influence with fake politeness and sweetness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affectedly' rearranges PROPER and SWEET together; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marketing jargon for children nagging parents to buy things, a persistent pressure.

clue.text: US singer-songwriter's notes, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: banknotes are an example of ready money

explanation.surface: Asking whether an American musician's notes are musical ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link ('is'); the question mark flags that notes are banknotes, not musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnny Cash was a country star, and banknotes are an example of money in hand.

clue.text: I end up struggling to catch winger, beginning to exhibit lack of skill

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the bird inside them
struggling letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a winger is a bird, here the tit

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to tackle a wide player shows their clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks like a footballer on the wing, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is incompetence, the absence of ability.

clue.text: See 20
Flying off

explanation.definitionFit: High means both far up in the air and starting to go rotten, as game does.

clue.text: Dog kennels in Germany, an architectural feature

indicators.note: to kennel is to house, so the dog encloses the letters

parts.note: bow-wow is a childish word for a dog
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Dog kennels in Germany described as a building feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kennels' is a verb: BOWWOW houses IN D.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay projecting from a wall, glazed, is a feature of buildings.

clue.text: Wet second and first

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A soggy thing ranked both runner-up and winner.
explanation.walkthrough: IST stands for 1st, with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means damp, slightly wet.

clue.text: Fruit grew hot

parts.note: rose means went up or grew
hip means fashionable, hot

explanation.definitionFit: The red seed pod of the rose plant is a fruit.

clue.text: Animal studied and highly-valued, it's said

indicators.note: the words are to be heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: read is studied, dear is highly valued

explanation.surface: An animal that has been studied and prized.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is a large species of deer, an example of a wild mammal.
